about.description: I'm a research networking systems engineer at ESnet, the Energy Sciences Network at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. I work on the software-defined networks and transfer tooling that keep high-energy physics data moving at petabyte scale.
details: My path ran through San Diego first: at the San Diego Supercomputer Center (UCSD) I led the SEAM project, worked on the National Research Platform's Kubernetes substrate and its FABRIC integration, taught the platform's intro courses, and spent a lot of late nights making P4 programs run on programmable FPGAs.

In September 2026 I joined ESnet at LBNL as a research networking systems engineer, remotely, from the same city I've been in. The fun part is data movement: software-defined networking for high-energy physics, SENSE orchestration, and interop between the tools scientists use to move files.

Off the clock I keep a long-lived list of side projects — network tooling, ML experiments, and the occasional impossible project — and I unironically believe every big idea deserves a small weekend prototype.
